title: Triangle-Free Chromatic Threshold
description: Let h_3(k) be the smallest n with a triangle-free graph on n vertices of chromatic number k. Find the asymptotic formula. Known: (1/2 - o(1))k^2 log k <= h_3(k) <= (1 + o(1))k^2 log k. Is h_3(k+1)/h_3(k) -> 1?

overview.historicalContext: The study of triangle-free graphs with high chromatic number began with Zykov (1949) and Mycielski (1955), who independently showed such graphs exist for every chromatic number. Mycielski's elegant inductive construction M_k produces triangle-free graphs with chi(M_k) = k, but |V(M_k)| grows exponentially. The quantitative question -- how many vertices are needed? -- became central. Graver and Yackel (1968) gave the first lower bound h_3(k) >> k^2 log k / log log k using probabilistic deletion. The modern bounds (1/2 - o(1))k^2 log k <= h_3(k) <= (1 + o(1))k^2 log k pin down the growth rate to Theta(k^2 log k), but the leading constant c remains open: it lies in [1/2, 1]. Erdos asked both for the exact asymptotic (determining c) and whether the ratio h_3(k+1)/h_3(k) converges to 1, which would imply the threshold grows smoothly. The problem connects to the Kim-type Ramsey bounds R(3,k) ~ k^2/(4 ln k), as h_3(k) and R(3,k) are closely related via Ramsey-theoretic duality: a triangle-free graph with chi >= k implies R(3,k) <= n. The problem is listed as Erdos Problem #1013 and is related to Problems #920 (K_r-free generalization) and #1104 (dual function f(n)).
overview.problemStatement: Find an asymptotic formula for $h_3(k)$, the smallest $n$ such that there exists a triangle-free graph on $n$ vertices with chromatic number $k$. Is $h_3(k+1)/h_3(k) \to 1$?
overview.proofStrategy: We formalize triangle-free graphs via the absence of 3-cliques using Mathlib's SimpleGraph, define proper colorings and chromatic number, and introduce the threshold function h_3(k) as a supremum. The main conjecture (asymptotic formula with limit c), ratio convergence, known upper and lower bounds, the Graver-Yackel historical bound, monotonicity, exact small cases (h_3(1) through h_3(4)), and Mycielski's existence construction are all stated as axioms. The formalization uses Filter.Tendsto for the limit statements.
keyInsights: The lower bound (1/2 - o(1))k^2 log k comes from probabilistic coloring: random partitions of vertices into k color classes yield proper colorings when the graph has few enough vertices relative to k
The upper bound (1 + o(1))k^2 log k uses explicit constructions via random triangle-free graphs or algebraic methods over finite fields
Mycielski's construction proves h_3(k) < infinity but gives exponential bounds (3 * 2^{k-2} - 1), far from the true Theta(k^2 log k) growth
The connection to Ramsey numbers: R(3,k) ~ k^2/(4 ln k) (Kim 1995, Bohman 2009) is closely related since a K_3-free graph with chi >= k on n vertices gives R(3,k) <= n
The exact small values h_3(3) = 5 (C_5) and h_3(4) = 11 (Grotzsch graph) are achieved by Mycielski graphs, which are the unique extremal graphs for these cases
Determining whether c = 1/2 or c = 1 would resolve a subtle question about the efficiency of probabilistic vs constructive methods for triangle-free chromatic number

sections.title: Header and Imports
sections.summary: Module docstring stating the problem with known bounds and references, followed by Mathlib imports for SimpleGraph, Clique, real analysis, logarithms, and tactics.

sections.title: Core Definitions
sections.summary: Defines IsTriangleFree (no 3-clique), HasProperColoring (vertex coloring with adjacency constraint), chromaticNumber (min colors needed), and triangleFreeChromThreshold h_3(k) as the minimum vertices for triangle-free chromatic number >= k.

sections.title: Main Conjecture
sections.summary: Two open questions: (1) the asymptotic formula h_3(k) ~ c k^2 log k for some constant c in [1/2, 1], formalized as Filter.Tendsto convergence; (2) ratio convergence h_3(k+1)/h_3(k) -> 1.

sections.title: Known Bounds
sections.summary: Three bounds: the modern lower bound (1/2 - o(1))k^2 log k from probabilistic coloring, the upper bound (1 + o(1))k^2 log k from explicit constructions, and the historical Graver-Yackel (1968) bound k^2 log k / log log k.

sections.title: Structural Properties and Small Cases
sections.summary: Monotonicity of h_3, exact values h_3(1)=1, h_3(2)=2, h_3(3)=5 (C_5), h_3(4)=11 (Grotzsch graph), and Mycielski's 1955 construction proving h_3(k) is finite for all k >= 2.

conclusion.summary: This formalization captures Erdos Problem #1013 on the triangle-free chromatic threshold h_3(k). The growth rate Theta(k^2 log k) is established by matching upper and lower bounds, but the leading constant c in [1/2, 1] and the ratio convergence h_3(k+1)/h_3(k) -> 1 remain open. The small cases via Mycielski graphs and the connection to Ramsey theory are also formalized.
conclusion.implications: Determining the exact asymptotic constant would resolve a fundamental question about the interplay between local structure (triangle-freeness) and global structure (chromatic number). It would also clarify the relationship between probabilistic existence proofs (giving the 1/2 lower bound) and explicit constructions (giving the 1 upper bound), potentially revealing whether constructive methods are optimal.
openQuestions: What is the exact asymptotic constant c in h_3(k) ~ c k^2 log k? Is it 1/2 or 1?
Is h_3(k+1)/h_3(k) -> 1, and can this be proved independently of the full asymptotic?
What about the K_r-free generalization h_r(k) for r >= 4? (Erdos Problem #920)
How does h_3(k) relate to R(3,k) ~ k^2/(4 ln k) quantitatively beyond the trivial h_3(k) >= R(3,k)?
Can algebraic constructions (e.g., over finite fields) improve on the probabilistic upper bound constant?
